vision.paraphrase: Getting the bank's export into one local file is the first goal; nothing else in the product can work until the rows are in the ledger.

conops.paraphrase: The user points the tool at the downloaded export and expects every row to land in the ledger, with a count confirming it.

vision.paraphrase: A single date format in the ledger is what lets later reports group by month without guessing how each bank writes dates.

conops.paraphrase: The user's banks export dates in two styles and they want one consistent form in the ledger without editing files by hand.

requirements.rationale: Whole cents avoid floating-point drift when totals are summed; the sign carries direction so a refund can net against spending later.

vision.paraphrase: Totals must be exact to the cent, and refunds must be able to net against spending, so amounts are stored as signed whole cents.

conops.paraphrase: The user expects the stored amounts to match the bank statement to the cent, whichever way the bank formats them.

requirements.rationale: The description is the user's evidence of what the bank reported; matching rules interpret it later without altering what is stored.

vision.paraphrase: The ledger is a faithful record of what the bank said, so the description text is never tidied on the way in.

conops.paraphrase: The user wants to recognise each line exactly as it appears on the bank statement when they look in the ledger.

vision.paraphrase: A budget that double-counts is worse than none; importing must be safe to repeat.

conops.paraphrase: The user downloads overlapping date ranges each month and expects rows already in the ledger to be skipped.
